name: Prussian Blue
poem: The first blue ever made by accident — a chemist reaching for red, and stumbling on the colour of the deep, the dusk, and the drawing board.

recipe.note: A very dark blue, deepened almost to black and cooled with a whisper of green.

lenses.label: Art History
lenses.intro: A pigment cheap enough to flood the world's skies, oceans and sorrows. Within a century of its invention it had crossed every sea on Earth.

entries.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
entries.blurb: Hokusai built the wave from imported Prussian blue — known in Japan as "bero-ai." The new synthetic pigment held its hue where traditional indigo faded, letting the foam claw at a permanent sky.

entries.title: The Starry Night
entries.blurb: The roiling night of Saint-Rémy is carried by Prussian blue and cobalt, swirled wet-into-wet from the asylum window before dawn.

entries.title: The Old Guitarist
entries.blurb: Picasso's Blue Period drowned its grief in this single cold pigment — poverty, hunger and isolation rendered almost monochrome.

lenses.label: Fashion
lenses.intro: Before it was a colour of leisure, blue was a colour of discipline — cut, pressed, and worn as authority.

entries.title: The Prussian Officer's Coat
entries.blurb: The deep uniform blue of the Prussian army lent the pigment its name and its bearing: severe, exact, unmistakable across a field.

entries.title: Bleu de Travail
entries.blurb: The chore jacket dyed working bodies the colour of the sky's indifference — hard-wearing, humble, now endlessly revived on the runway.

entries.title: The Navy Suit
entries.blurb: No colour signals quiet authority like a dark navy — formal without the finality of black, the default uniform of trust.

lenses.label: Nature
lenses.intro: True blue is vanishingly rare in the living world. Most of what we call blue is a trick of structure, not pigment.

entries.title: The Indigo Bunting
entries.blurb: The bird carries no blue pigment at all — microscopic feather structure scatters light, painting it sky-blue only when the sun agrees.

entries.title: The Blue Hour
entries.blurb: The window after sunset when the sun lights only the upper atmosphere, draining the world to a single saturated, sourceless blue.

entries.title: The Bathyal Zone
entries.blurb: Red light dies first in seawater; blue travels deepest. Past a thousand metres, blue is the last colour, then none at all.

lenses.label: Pop Culture
lenses.intro: The pigment quietly built the modern world's documents — and, improbably, became a life-saving drug.

entries.title: The Blueprint
entries.blurb: Architecture and engineering were copied for a century in Prussian blue. The word "blueprint" outlived the chemistry that made it.

entries.title: Photographs of British Algae
entries.blurb: Often called the first book illustrated with photographs — ghostly white seaweed laid on fields of Prussian blue.

entries.title: Radiogardase
entries.blurb: Pharmaceutical-grade Prussian blue binds thallium and radioactive cesium in the gut — the same molecule that colours a blueprint.

lenses.label: Etymology
lenses.intro: A colour named for an army, born from a botched batch of red dye in a Berlin laboratory.

entries.title: Berliner Blau
entries.blurb: Colour-maker Johann Jacob Diesbach was attempting a red lake when contaminated potash turned his batch a brilliant, unexpected blue.

entries.title: "Preußisch Blau"
entries.blurb: The pigment took the name of the state whose military wore it — the first colour named after a nation rather than a place or a plant.

entries.title: "Bero-ai"
entries.blurb: Imported through Nagasaki, the foreign blue entered Japanese as a loanword — "berorin ai," Berlin indigo — before transforming ukiyo-e.

lenses.label: Symbolism
lenses.intro: Across cultures the colour holds two opposite truths at once: distance and depth, sadness and trust.

entries.title: Feeling Blue
entries.blurb: The Western shorthand for sorrow. Picasso painted it; the blues sang it. A colour cool enough to stand in for grief itself.

entries.title: The Unconscious
entries.blurb: Blue recedes — the colour of horizons, dreams and the parts of the mind we cannot reach. We move "into the blue."

entries.title: True Blue
entries.blurb: The same recession reads as steadiness: the loyal friend, the dependable institution, the colour chosen by banks and nations.
